question: Why was the emailservice pod replaced?
situation: emailservice had hpa.minReplicas 1 but replicas 2 in the chart. Every ~5 minutes the HPA scaled the Deployment 2 -> 1 ('All metrics below target'), and seconds later Argo CD self-heal restored the 2 replicas rendered from values.yaml, so the ReplicaSet deleted its newest pod and then created a new one. Fixed by omitting spec.replicas from Deployments that have an HPA (branch fix/hpa-omit-replicas).

recorded_tool_output.note: Captured on 2026-10-04 with the pre-'controller events first' formatter, as cut to 6000 characters by the agent. Reuse it to replay this case once the live cluster no longer shows the cycle.

key_evidence: HorizontalPodAutoscaler/emailservice SuccessfulRescale (x18): New size: 1; reason: All metrics below target
Deployment/emailservice ScalingReplicaSet (x18): Scaled down replica set emailservice-7959ddb655 from 2 to 1
Deployment/emailservice ScalingReplicaSet (x19): Scaled up replica set emailservice-7959ddb655 from 1 to 2 - with no HPA event asking for 2
Each cycle: Killing + SuccessfulDelete of the newest pod, then SuccessfulCreate, Scheduled, Started of a new one, about every 5 minutes
Readiness probe failures (x2-x3) appear only in the first seconds after each new pod starts
The long-running pod (about 1h old) is never the one deleted
expected_diagnosis: The pod was deleted by a controller, not by a probe, and it is a repeating cycle (x18/x19). Scale-down half: the HPA set the size to 1 because all metrics were below target and its minReplicas is 1. Scale-up half: the Deployment was scaled back to 2 with no HPA event asking for it - Argo CD self-heal restoring the replicas: 2 that the chart renders from values.yaml. The HPA (min 1) and the chart's replica count (2) conflict, so the two keep undoing each other. On each scale-down the ReplicaSet deletes its newest pod, which is why the old pod survives. The readiness failures are normal startup and not a cause.

must_explain: the HPA scale-down to 1 (All metrics below target / minReplicas 1)
the scale-up back to 2, and that it repeats (x18/x19)
the conflict between the HPA and the chart's replica count, restored by Argo CD self-heal / GitOps reconciliation
must_not: name readiness probes (or any probe) as the root cause
claim the HPA chose or removed a particular (unhealthy) pod
explain the surviving pod by its node or health

must_not_contain: readiness probe timeouts are the root cause

expected_tool_calls: read_repo_file helm/online-boutique/values.yaml or list_hpas, to confirm replicas 2 vs minReplicas 1

runs.answer: The pod was killed because its readiness probe failed.
runs.why_wrong: A failing readiness probe never kills a pod. It looked only at the pod's own events, not the Deployment, ReplicaSet and HPA.

runs.agent_version: after commit a1b83a2 (prompt guidance, list_events app=)
runs.answer: Identified the HPA scale-down, but called readiness probe timeouts 'the root cause', said the HPA 'removed the unhealthy pod', and said the old pod survived because it is on a different node.
runs.why_wrong: Ignored 'Scaled up replica set from 1 to 2 (x19)' and never asked what keeps restoring 2 replicas. The readiness failures occur only in each pod's first seconds. The HPA only sets a count; the ReplicaSet deletes its newest pod. Neither the HPA choosing a pod nor the node explanation is supported by any tool result.

runs.agent_version: after commit a1b83a2, Sonnet model (per the file name)
runs.answer: HPA scale-down and Argo CD self-heal restoring 2 replicas, repeating all hour; readiness failures only at startup and explicitly not the cause; noted Deployment generation 40 vs 2 elsewhere.
runs.verdict: Mostly passes. Gap: could not confirm replicas: 2 in values.yaml because read_repo_file output was truncated before the emailservice block, so the Git side was inferred from the Deployment's desired count. Fixed by read_repo_file search/start_line. Its suggested fix (align replicas with minReplicas in values) treats the symptom; the chart fix removes the conflict for every HPA service.
